title: Silent Error Suppression in Long-Running Background Loops
pattern: Catching and discarding all errors in a core background process loop, allowing the loop to continue spinning endlessly without logging or alerting.
why_bad: If a database connection fails, the background job spins in a tight loop at 100% CPU utilization, generating no value, exhausting resources, and hiding the service failure from monitoring tools.
detection: A `loop` containing a catch-all match `Err(_)` that does not contain break logic, sleep modifiers, or error reporting / metrics updates.
counterexample: Retrying a highly transient operation with explicit loop counters and backoffs.
fix: If a background process fails persistently, log the failure, increment an error metric, and either shut down the process or enter a backed-off retry state.
